newsitem.title: USA: U.S. militia fights on the fringe for God, freedom.
newsitem.headline: U.S. militia fights on the fringe for God, freedom.

text.p: Every year, this small U.S. city is invaded by men in army fatigues who rail against a global conspiracy to take away their guns, their God and their property.

The mayor of Lansing raises the blue U.N. flag outside city hall in an annual ceremony to celebrate the founding of the world body -- drawing protests from U.S. militia groups who see the United Nations as a sinister left-wing plot to establish a global government.
Protected by barriers and a line of 30 police in riot gear, Mayor David Hollister hoisted the flag once again on Thursday as some 300 militia members booed and called him a traitor.
"We want our country back and we want them to take that piece of crap down," said Tom Wayne, one of the leaders of the Michigan Militia, gesturing at the fluttering blue flag.
"As a Vietnam veteran I fought for this country and I am ready to fight again," said Wayne, 50. "We are on the verge of civil war."
Mainstream America may be looking to the U.S. presidential elections in less than two weeks time, but the militia is getting ready for the apocalypse.

Hundreds of groups are scattered across the United States, mainly in remote rural areas. They call themselves true patriots, wear uniforms, arm themselves and train to fight for their view of the American way.
The militia groups and the "angry white men" who swell their ranks shot to international prominence last year after the bombing in Oklahoma in which nearly 170 people were killed.
Most oppose gun control, U.S. involvement abroad, foreign trade agreements and taxes. Critics say they are no more than racist conspiracy theorists.
The Michigan Militia claims between 12,000 and 15,000 members but far fewer turned up in Lansing on Thursday to protest -- unarmed -- at the white-domed Capitol building opposite city hall.

Some brought their children and wives to hear speakers including a local militia commander who won loud applause by using the U.N. flag to blow his nose. A pastor denounced the United Nations as "the devil's handmaiden", to loud cries of "Amen" and "That's right".
A four-strong honour guard paraded amid a sea of U.S. flags and a man walked in the crowd with a Doberman that had a dog collar made of rifle bullets.
Stalls did a brisk business selling books on wilderness survival techniques and a mail-order catalogue from the Montana Militia offering suits to protect against chemical weapons.

Many of the men seemed to be in their 40s and 50s. Many fought in the Vietnam war more than 20 years ago -- rough, bearded types who bear the scars of the worst U.S. humiliation this century. None showed interest in the forthcoming presidential election.
"One's as bad as the other," said George Ettinger, 51, with a shrug.
Mayor Hollister said he took the threat of violence seriously and that local police had stopped a car last week driven by militia members, to find a trunk full of semi- automatic weapons.
"It's not a joke," he told Reuters in an interview.

Disillusion with the established political system in the United States has caused voter apathy and thrown up maverick figures like presidential contender Ross Perot, who want to change the system. Hollister, a Democrat, believes the militia is part of that disenchantment.
"I believe it's growing," he said. "It's an extreme symptom of the anti-establishment, anti-government feeling in this country."
